source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

verses.rationale: Keeps slave and apostle identities and their stated purpose.
verses.before: Paul, a slave of God and apostle of Jesus Christ, for the trust of God’s chosen people and the knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness,
verses.after: Paul, a slave of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, for the faith of God's chosen people and their knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness,
verses.tsw_comparator: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, for the sake of the faith of God’s elect and their knowledge of the truth, which accords with godliness,

verses.rationale: Preserves hope, divine truthfulness and pretemporal promise.
verses.before: in hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before eternal times
verses.after: in the hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before eternal times
verses.tsw_comparator: in hope of eternal life, which God, who never lies, promised before the ages began

verses.rationale: Keeps appointed timing, preaching and commanded stewardship.
verses.before: and revealed at the proper time in his word through the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior,
verses.after: and revealed at the proper time in his word through the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior,
verses.tsw_comparator: and at the proper time manifested in his word through the proclamation with which I have been entrusted by the command of God our Savior;

verses.rationale: Retains kinship, shared faith and the Savior title applied to Christ.
verses.before: to Titus, my true child according to our common trust: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
verses.after: to Titus, my true child in our common faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
verses.tsw_comparator: to Titus, my true child in a common faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.

verses.rationale: Keeps named island, unfinished order and town-by-town appointments.
verses.before: I left you in Crete for this reason: so that you might put in order what remained and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.
verses.after: I left you in Crete for this reason: to set right what remained and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is why I left you in Crete, so that you might put what remained into order, and appoint elders in every town as I directed you—

verses.rationale: Preserves male marital idiom and the ambiguous believing/faithful description.
verses.before: An elder must be above accusation, faithful to one spouse, with believing children who are not accused of reckless living or rebellion.
verses.after: An elder must be beyond accusation, a one-woman man, with faithful children not accused of wild living or rebellion.
verses.tsw_comparator: if anyone is above reproach, the husband of one wife, and his children are believers and not open to the charge of debauchery or insubordination.

verses.rationale: Keeps stewardship and all five prohibitions.
verses.before: For an overseer, as God’s steward, must be above accusation—not arrogant, quick-tempered, addicted to wine, violent, or greedy for dishonest gain,
verses.after: For an overseer, as God's steward, must be beyond accusation—not self-willed, quick-tempered, addicted to wine, violent or greedy for dishonest gain,
verses.tsw_comparator: For an overseer, as God’s steward, must be above reproach. He must not be arrogant or quick-tempered or a drunkard or violent or greedy for gain,

verses.rationale: Preserves all six positive qualities.
verses.before: but hospitable, loving what is good, self-controlled, righteous, holy, disciplined,
verses.after: but hospitable, loving what is good, self-controlled, just, holy and disciplined,
verses.tsw_comparator: but hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined.

verses.rationale: Keeps holding, health metaphor and two teaching functions.
verses.before: holding firmly to the trustworthy word according to the teaching, so that they may be able both to encourage with sound teaching and to correct those who contradict it.
verses.after: holding firmly to the trustworthy word according to the teaching, so that he may be able both to encourage with sound teaching and to correct those who contradict it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He must hold firm to the trustworthy word as taught, so that he may be able both to give instruction in sound doctrine and also to rebuke those who contradict it.

verses.rationale: Retains three descriptions and specified subgroup.
verses.before: For there are many rebellious people, empty talkers, and deceivers, especially those from the circumcision group.
verses.after: For there are many rebellious people, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those from the circumcision group.
verses.tsw_comparator: For there are many who are insubordinate, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision party.

verses.rationale: Keeps forceful response, household harm and financial motive.
verses.before: They must be silenced because they are overturning whole households by teaching what they should not for shameful gain.
verses.after: They must be silenced, because they overturn whole households by teaching what they should not for shameful gain.
verses.tsw_comparator: They must be silenced, since they are upsetting whole households by teaching for shameful gain what they ought not to teach.

verses.rationale: Preserves the quoted ethnic insult, speaker relation and animal/bodily rhetoric.
verses.before: One of their own prophets said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons.”
verses.after: One of their own, a prophet of theirs, said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy bellies.”
verses.tsw_comparator: One of the Cretans, a prophet of their own, said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons.”

verses.rationale: Retains the letter's endorsement, severity and corrective aim.
verses.before: This testimony is true. Therefore correct them sharply so that they may become sound in the trust,
verses.after: This testimony is true. Therefore, rebuke them sharply so that they may become sound in the faith,
verses.tsw_comparator: This testimony is true. Therefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,

verses.rationale: Keeps the specific polemical labels without generalizing beyond the opponents.
verses.before: not paying attention to Jewish myths and commands of people who turn away from the truth.
verses.after: not paying attention to Jewish myths and commands of people who turn away from the truth.
verses.tsw_comparator: not devoting themselves to Jewish myths and the commands of people who turn away from the truth.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated purity/defilement and paired inner faculties.
verses.before: To the pure, all things are pure, but to those who are defiled and do not trust, nothing is pure; both their mind and conscience are defiled.
verses.after: To the pure, everything is pure; but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. Both their mind and conscience are defiled.
verses.tsw_comparator: To the pure, all things are pure, but to the defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure; but both their minds and their consciences are defiled.

verses.rationale: Keeps word/deed contradiction and all three harsh judgments.
verses.before: They profess to know God, but by their works they deny him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
verses.after: They profess to know God, but deny him by their actions. They are detestable, disobedient and unfit for any good work.
verses.tsw_comparator: They profess to know God, but they deny him by their works. They are detestable, disobedient, unfit for any good work.

verses.rationale: Retains contrast and health metaphor.
verses.before: But you, speak what fits sound teaching.
verses.after: But you must speak what is consistent with sound teaching.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for you, teach what accords with sound doctrine.

verses.rationale: Keeps age/gender specificity and full sixfold character.
verses.before: Older men are to be sober, dignified, self-controlled, sound in trust, love, and endurance.
verses.after: Older men are to be sober, dignified, self-controlled and sound in faith, love and endurance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Older men are to be sober-minded, dignified, self-controlled, sound in faith, in love, and in steadfastness.

verses.rationale: Retains female group, slavery metaphor and teaching role.
verses.before: Older women likewise are to be reverent in behavior, not slanderers or enslaved to much wine, but teachers of what is good,
verses.after: Older women likewise are to be reverent in conduct, not slanderers or enslaved to much wine, but teachers of what is good,
verses.tsw_comparator: Older women likewise are to be reverent in behavior, not slanderers or slaves to much wine. They are to teach what is good,

verses.rationale: Keeps intergenerational instruction and both family loves.
verses.before: so that they may train the younger women to love their husbands and children,
verses.after: so that they may train the young women to love their husbands and children,
verses.tsw_comparator: and so train the young women to love their husbands and children,

verses.rationale: Preserves gendered household expectations and reputational rationale.
verses.before: to be self-controlled, pure, workers at home, kind, and responsive to their own husbands, so that God’s word is not slandered.
verses.after: to be self-controlled, pure, workers at home, good and submissive to their own husbands, so that God's word may not be slandered.
verses.tsw_comparator: to be self-controlled, pure, working at home, kind, and subject to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be reviled.

verses.rationale: Keeps male age group and concise exhortation.
verses.before: Likewise urge younger men to be self-controlled.
verses.after: Likewise, urge the younger men to be self-controlled.
verses.tsw_comparator: Likewise, urge the younger men to be self-controlled.

verses.rationale: Retains personal example and two teaching qualities.
verses.before: In everything present yourself as an example of good works, showing integrity and dignity in your teaching,
verses.after: In everything, present yourself as an example of good works. In your teaching show integrity and dignity,
verses.tsw_comparator: Show yourself in all respects to be a model of good works, and in your teaching show integrity, dignity,

verses.rationale: Keeps health metaphor, public scrutiny and corporate reputation.
verses.before: and sound speech that cannot be condemned, so that an opponent may be put to shame, having nothing bad to say about us.
verses.after: with sound speech that cannot be condemned, so that an opponent may be ashamed, having nothing bad to say about us.
verses.tsw_comparator: and sound speech that cannot be condemned, so that an opponent may be put to shame, having nothing evil to say about us.

verses.rationale: Names enslaved people and masters and preserves the coercive submission command.
verses.before: Slaves are to be responsive to their own masters in everything, seeking to please them, not talking back,
verses.after: Slaves are to submit to their own masters in everything, to be pleasing and not talk back,
verses.tsw_comparator: Slaves are to be subject to their own masters in everything; they are to be well-pleasing, not argumentative,

verses.rationale: Keeps prohibited appropriation, trustworthiness and adornment metaphor.
verses.before: not stealing, but showing complete good faith, so that in everything they may adorn the teaching of God our Savior.
verses.after: not stealing, but demonstrating complete good faith, so that in everything they may adorn the teaching about God our Savior.
verses.tsw_comparator: not pilfering, but showing all good faith, so that in everything they may adorn the doctrine of God our Savior.

verses.rationale: Preserves grace's epiphany and universal reach.
verses.before: For God’s grace has appeared, bringing salvation for all people,
verses.after: For God's grace has appeared, bringing salvation to all people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people,

verses.rationale: Keeps instruction, two renunciations and three positive adverbs.
verses.before: training us to deny ungodliness and worldly desires and to live self-controlled, righteous, and godly lives in the present age,
verses.after: It trains us to renounce ungodliness and worldly desires and to live self-controlled, just and godly lives in the present age,
verses.tsw_comparator: training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age,

verses.rationale: Retains hope/appearing and the dense divine title.
verses.before: while we wait for the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,
verses.after: while we wait for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: waiting for our blessed hope, the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ,

verses.rationale: Keeps self-gift, redemption, purification and eager action.
verses.before: who gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and cleanse for himself a people as his own possession, zealous for good works.
verses.after: He gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and cleanse for himself a people of his own, zealous for good works.
verses.tsw_comparator: who gave himself for us that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a people of his own who are zealous for good deeds.

verses.rationale: Retains all three speech acts and authority.
verses.before: Speak these things, encourage, and correct with all authority. Let no one disregard you.
verses.after: Speak these things, encourage and correct with complete authority. Let no one disregard you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Declare these things; exhort and rebuke with all authority. Let no one disregard you.

verses.rationale: Keeps political submission and readiness.
verses.before: Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to obey, to be ready for every good work,
verses.after: Remind them to submit to rulers and authorities, to obey and to be ready for every good work,
verses.tsw_comparator: Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,

verses.rationale: Preserves universal speech restraint and three relational qualities.
verses.before: to slander no one, to avoid fighting, to be gentle, showing complete courtesy toward all people.
verses.after: to slander no one, to be peaceable and gentle, showing complete humility toward everyone.
verses.tsw_comparator: to speak evil of no one, to avoid quarreling, to be gentle, and to show perfect courtesy toward all people.

verses.rationale: Keeps shared past, slavery metaphor and reciprocal hatred.
verses.before: For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, deceived, enslaved to various desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hated and hating one another.
verses.after: For we too were once foolish, disobedient and deceived, enslaved to various desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful and hating one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, led astray, slaves to various passions and pleasures, passing our days in malice and envy, despicable, hating one another.

verses.rationale: Retains epiphany language and philanthropic term.
verses.before: But when the kindness and love for humanity of God our Savior appeared,
verses.after: But when the kindness and love for humanity of God our Savior appeared,
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared,

verses.rationale: Preserves denial, mercy and paired washing/renewal means.
verses.before: he saved us—not because of works we had done in righteousness, but according to his mercy—through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
verses.after: he saved us—not because of righteous works we had done, but according to his mercy—through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
verses.tsw_comparator: he saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water[a] of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.

verses.rationale: Keeps Spirit as poured gift and Christ's mediation.
verses.before: whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
verses.after: whom he poured out richly on us through Jesus Christ our Savior,
verses.tsw_comparator: whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior,

verses.rationale: Retains legal status, inheritance and hope.
verses.before: so that, having been set right by his grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
verses.after: so that, justified by his grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that being justified by his grace we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

verses.rationale: Keeps formal saying, emphatic instruction and practical benefit.
verses.before: This saying is trustworthy, and I want you to insist on these things so that those who have trusted God may be careful to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and beneficial for people.
verses.after: This saying is trustworthy, and I want you to insist on these things so that those who have believed God may be careful to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and beneficial for people.
verses.tsw_comparator: The saying is true. I desire that you insist on these things, so that those who have come to believe in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works; these things are excellent and profitable to everyone.

verses.rationale: Preserves full list and both evaluations.
verses.before: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, quarrels, and fights about the Law, because they are unprofitable and worthless.
verses.after: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, quarrels and fights about the law, because they are unprofitable and empty.
verses.tsw_comparator: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, dissensions, and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and worthless.

verses.rationale: Keeps two-stage correction and factional behavior.
verses.before: After a first and second warning, have nothing more to do with a divisive person,
verses.after: After a first and second warning, reject a divisive person,
verses.tsw_comparator: As for a person who stirs up division, after warning him once and then twice, have nothing more to do with him,

verses.rationale: Retains moral distortion and inward verdict.
verses.before: knowing that such a person has become twisted and is sinning, being self-condemned.
verses.after: knowing that such a person is warped and sins, being self-condemned.
verses.tsw_comparator: knowing that such a person is warped and sinful; he is self-condemned.

verses.rationale: Keeps both possible messengers, destination and seasonal plan.
verses.before: When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to spend the winter there.
verses.after: When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to spend the winter there.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.

verses.rationale: Retains names, profession and material support.
verses.before: Diligently help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way so that they lack nothing.
verses.after: Diligently help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, so that they lack nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do your best to speed Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way; see that they lack nothing.

verses.rationale: Keeps learned provision and fruit metaphor.
verses.before: Our people must also learn to devote themselves to good works for urgent needs, so that they will not be unfruitful.
verses.after: Our people too must learn to devote themselves to good works for urgent needs, so that they will not be unfruitful.
verses.tsw_comparator: And let our people learn to devote themselves to good works, so as to help cases of urgent need, and not be unfruitful.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three closing sentences and plural blessing.
verses.before: Everyone with me greets you. Greet those who love us in the trust. Grace be with all of you.
verses.after: Everyone with me greets you. Greet those who love us in faith. Grace be with all of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: All who are with me send greetings to you. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all.
